name: Isolated Radio-Ulnar Synostosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnosis of Isolated Radio-Ulnar Synostosis

criteria.description: Congenital osseous fusion between the radius and ulna
Limited or absent forearm pronation and supination
No associated skeletal abnormalities or syndromic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital osseous fusion between radius and ulna with restricted forearm pronation and supination, without other skeletal or syndromic anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may be considered to exclude syndromic forms.

occasional.symptomName: Abnormality of the musculature of the upper arm

imaging: X-ray showing osseous fusion between proximal radius and ulna
CT scan for detailed bone anatomy and extent of synostosis
genetic: Usually sporadic; genetic testing to exclude syndromic causes such as Holt-Oram syndrome or other skeletal dysplasias
other: Physical examination revealing fixed forearm position and restricted rotation

distinguishingFeatures: History of forearm trauma or fracture
Radiological evidence of post-injury bone bridging
Presence of additional skeletal or systemic anomalies
Genetic mutations associated with syndromes (e.g., Holt-Oram syndrome)

redFlags: Development of neurological symptoms such as numbness or weakness
Presence of systemic features suggesting syndromic involvement
references: Bauer AS, et al. Congenital Radio-Ulnar Synostosis: Clinical and Radiological Features. J Hand Surg Am. 2018;43(4):345-351.
Orphanet Report Series: Radio-Ulnar Synostosis. Orphanet. 2021.
Flatt AE. The Care of Congenital Hand Anomalies. 2nd ed. 1999.
